ui.title: The plot
ui.sub: Search · Planning analysis · Due diligence · Acquisition
ui.goal: Buy a plot that can be built on, at the price the project can bear, with no hidden encumbrances.

vo: Module one: the plot.
The objective: buy a plot that can be built on, at the price the project can bear, and with no hidden encumbrances.

ui.title: Four steps
steps: Define the product and find the plot
ui.result: Plot conveyed by deed to the SPE, or an option to buy signed

vo: There are four steps.
You define the product and find the plot.
You work out what you can build.
You carry out the due diligence.
And you close the purchase.
By the end, the plot is conveyed by deed to your company, or you hold a signed option to buy.

ui.title: The product sheet
ui.note: One page: the filter you will look at every plot through.

vo: Before you search, define what you are going to develop.
The type of development, the target buyers, the homes and their layouts, the quality of finishes, and the target sale price.
It all fits on a one-page product sheet: the filter you will look at every plot through.

ui.title: What you are looking for
ui.yesNote: The only land you can apply for a licence on without urbanisation works first
ui.noNote: Reparcelling, land transfers and urbanisation works · years

vo: What you are looking for is consolidated urban land:
with road access, water, sewerage and electricity, and with set building lines.
It is the only land you can apply for a licence on without carrying out urbanisation works first.
Developable land is cheaper, but it needs reparcelling, land transfers and urbanisation works, and it takes years. It is not for your first development.
The channels, from most to least profitable, start with your own network: notaries, lawyers, property managers.
Then the active search in the general plan: you find blocks with unused buildability, and you write to the owners.
And after that, portals, servicers, auctions, and public land.
Before you spend more time on it, apply the ten-minute filter.
Buildability, times the sale price in the area: that is your revenue. Compare it with the asking price.
If the land is more than thirty percent of the revenue, drop it, unless the location is prime.
Step two: what you can build.
The autonomous community makes the planning law, and the town hall applies its general plan and its bylaws.
That is where you get the parameters. Buildability: one thousand square metres of land, times two, gives two thousand square metres of floor area.
And then, the maximum height, the site coverage, the setbacks, and the parking spaces required.

ui.title: In practice
cards: From the municipal or regional viewer
From the town hall, in writing
ui.warn: Calculate with the surveyed area, not the cadastral one

vo: In practice: download the plan, ask your architect for a massing study, and ask the town hall for the planning certificate in writing.
And calculate with the surveyed area, not the cadastral one.

ui.title: Due diligence
ui.fix: If not: a survey, and regularise before you buy

vo: Step three: due diligence, so you buy without surprises.
Get the nota simple, and the certificate of title and encumbrances.
And check that the Land Registry, the Cadastre and what is on the ground all match. If they do not, commission a topographic survey, and regularise before you buy.

ui.title: Check as well
chips: IBI debts · the property is liable
ui.cost: Reinforcing the grid: tens of thousands of euros, and months

vo: Check the property tax debts as well, because the property itself is liable for them; the occupants; and the geotechnics, if you are building basements.
And the capacity of the utility connections: reinforcing the grid can mean tens of thousands of euros, and months of delay.
Step four: the purchase.

You can buy outright; with an option to buy, paying a premium of three to ten percent, for a term of six to twenty-four months; subject to a condition; with a deposit; or by swapping the plot for future homes.
And look at how it is taxed.
If a business sells building land: VAT, which you deduct, plus stamp duty on the deed.
If a private individual sells: transfer tax, which you do not get back.

ui.title: The SPE
ui.bank: Without real equity, no bank will lend

vo: Buy in the name of a special purpose company: one limited company per development isolates the risks, and makes it easier for partners to come in.
The minimum capital is one euro, but a bank will not lend to a company without real equity.

ui.title: Typical mistakes
items: Falling in love with the location without running the numbers
Buying “developable” land thinking it can be built on
Buying in your own name and contributing it later: taxed twice

vo: The typical mistakes:
falling in love with the location without running the numbers;
buying developable land thinking it can be built on;
and buying in your own name to contribute it to the company later: you are taxed twice.
